description: Engine registry for Meera. Each entry is an open-source AI assistant that Meera can route requests to. Pinned commits keep the install reproducible.

engines.name: Open Interpreter
engines.role: Hands. Turns plain language into real actions on the machine — files, terminals, scripts. This is the engine that makes Meera feel like JARVIS rather than a chatbot.
engines.install_hint: pip install open-interpreter   (needs an LLM backend: OPENAI_API_KEY, or a local Ollama/LM Studio server)
engines.notes: Requires an LLM provider for actual execution. Meera's gateway loads it lazily, so a missing package never blocks the HUD.

engines.name: Leon
engines.role: Skill library. A mature personal-assistant framework with a wake-word pipeline and dozens of pluggable skills — the closest open-source sibling to a home JARVIS.
engines.install_hint: cd integrations/vendor/leon && npm install && npm run build
engines.notes: Runs as its own Node service on port 1337. Meera can proxy to it later via adapters/leon.py.

engines.name: JARVIS (HuggingGPT)
engines.role: Planner. Uses a large language model to decompose a request into subtasks, then dispatches each to a specialist model from Hugging Face. This is the multi-model brain.
engines.notes: Research code from Microsoft. Needs an OpenAI key plus Hugging Face endpoints to actually plan tasks.

engines.name: Faster-Whisper
engines.role: Ears. Runs OpenAI's Whisper through CTranslate2 — up to 4x faster with far less memory. Gives Meera reliable, private, fully offline voice input.
engines.notes: Downloads a Whisper model on first use (tiny ~75MB, base ~145MB, small ~480MB).

engines.name: openWakeWord
engines.role: Ear-drums. Runs a tiny neural net locally so the phrase "Meera" wakes the assistant without sending any audio to the cloud.
engines.notes: Bonus engine. The HUD already supports wake word through the browser's SpeechRecognition; this one is for offline/desktop builds.
